articles.title: Final Countdown; California Leavin'; Best of the Fests; There's a Plan?
articles.summary:
Final Countdown; California Leavin'; Best of the Fests; There's a Plan?

Weekender: What's interesting and what matters in Hollywood.
View on web
September 19, 2026
Is Hollywood's biggest prizefight about to end in a handshake? It's no understatement to say that the industry may be reshaped by whatever details are being hammered out in
David Ellison
and
Rob Bonta
's war rooms this weekend. —
Erik Hayden
Ticker:
Brad Pitt
won't let
World War Z
go;
Gavin Newsom
boosts post-production;
Robbie Whelan
tackles
Bob Iger
;
Adam Smith
is Disney's new streaming boss.
Final Countdown
Time flies. It's been
more than a year
since
David Ellison
, fresh off acquiring Paramount, launched a bid to seize Warner Bros. Discovery last September. Since then, he tapped his father
Larry Ellison
's Oracle riches, improbably outlasted
Ted Sarandos
and Netflix, wooed
Donald Trump
's team to wave along the deal and courted governments abroad to greenlight his $111 billion merger with minor concessions made. Then came
Rob Bonta
and the California attorney general's posse of
12 states
who filed suit with plans to block the deal, as the last obstacle.
If
leaks
are to be believed, we're in the ninth inning of settlement talks. Which leads to a big question:
What is Bonta securing from this fight?
The AG has been on a media blitz vowing not to strike a deal unless there's real "structural remedies." Much of the chatter so far on what that means, in practice, has centered on a potential sell off of cable channels (say,
HGTVs
,
Comedy Centrals
,
Food Networks
and
TNTs
of the world).
But the rubber meets the road in the nitty gritty. Will Bonta strike a deal to require Warner Bros. and Paramount to operate as
independent entities
for a certain time period? Secure commitments for the combined entity to continue
licensing outside content
? Prod Ellison to up his commitment to releasing a combined 30 films a year for, say,

instead of 3? Cleave off or require independent oversight of news giants l
